claims.canonical_claim_text: Declared checkpoint hashes and Git presence guarantee scientific reproducibility.
canonical_limitations: Configuration declarations and code presence do not prove actual assets, rights, source lineage, GT or repeated experiments
claims.manuscript_wording: Provenance uncertainty changes the interpretation of a metric even when its numeric value is transcribed accurately. A leakage-flagged still-image result cannot answer an event-independent question, and a validation/test-label conflict cannot be resolved by choosing the higher score. Likewise, precise configuration hashes improve reference specificity without proving that the specified checkpoint was available or used. These distinctions explain why the historical notes belong in limitations rather than a new performance-results section.
required_qualification: Configuration declarations and code presence do not prove actual assets, rights, source lineage, GT or repeated experiments

canonical_limitations: Cooperative software behavior; no OS isolation, genuine deployment or institutional approval established
claims.manuscript_wording: Verification, readiness and authorization answer different questions (Table 2). Document submission initiates a reviewable record. Verification requires attributable evidence and a competent verifier. Purpose acceptance concerns a specific supported use. Readiness evaluates prerequisites, while authorization is an exact operation decision. Execution and its output provenance follow only within that authorized scope. [D2, D6, D9]
